zh: 1 引言：“一般货币”的社会关系
en: 1 Introduction: The Social Relations of ‘Money in General’

children: 不久前，《经济与社会》主持了一场关于货币概念化的理论争论，一方是泽利泽，另一方是法恩与拉帕维察斯。
更具体些说，泽利泽拒绝新古典经济学（以及某些社会学）对货币的理论化，声称“一般货币”概念无效。相反，法恩与拉帕维察斯捍卫“一般货币”概念，并从马克思主义视角加以分析。
A short while ago,
Economy and Society
hosted a theoretical debate regarding the conceptualisation of money between, on the one hand, Zelizer and, on the other, Fine and Lapavitsas.

To be a little more specific, Zelizer rejected the theorising of money by neoclassical economics (and by some sociology) and claimed that the concept of ‘money in general’ is invalid. In contrast, Fine and Lapavitsas defend the concept of ‘money in general’ and analysed it from a Marxist perspective.
英厄姆介入争论，认为双方都需要“理清”，尽管他在主要争点上又“强烈赞同”法恩与拉帕维察斯。
特别是，他批评法恩与拉帕维察斯借助马克思的著作，而他认为这些著作无法支撑“一般货币”理论。使事情更复杂的是，英厄姆还宣称自己“与法恩和拉帕维察斯对马克思货币概念的解释不一致”。
简言之，对英厄姆而言，法恩与拉帕维察斯强调“一般货币”的重要性是对的，但依赖马克思是错的，而且他们还误读了马克思。
Intervening in the debate, Ingham has found both sides in need of ‘untangling’, despite also ‘strongly agreeing’ with Fine and Lapavitsas on the main issue in contention.

In particular, he criticised Fine and Lapavitsas for drawing on Marx’s work, which he considered to be incapable of supporting a theory of ‘money in general’. Complicating things further, Ingham also declared himself ‘at odds with Fine and Lapavitsas’s interpretation of Marx’s conception of money’.
For Ingham, in short, Fine and Lapavitsas are right to stress the importance of ‘money in general’, but wrong to rely on Marx, whom they misinterpret to boot.
值得注意的是，英厄姆没有认真把握法恩与拉帕维察斯的分析就拒绝了它。他的真正目的是提出一种与德国历史学派和后凯恩斯主义相联系的“一般货币”替代理论。显然，法恩与拉帕维察斯（以及泽利泽）忽视了这一替代理论，结果过度聚焦商品货币，忽略信用货币，无视货币作为“支付承诺”所内在的社会关系。

It is notable that Ingham rejected Fine and Lapavitsas’s analysis without properly getting to grips with it. His true aim was to present an alternative theory of ‘money in general’, associated with the German Historical School and post-Keynesianism. Apparently, Fine and Lapavitsas (and Zelizer) neglected this alternative and, as a result, focused excessively on commodity money, while ignoring credit money and disregarding the social relations inherent to money as ‘promise to pay’.
这一忽视的指责至少可以说是令人惊讶的，因为争论一方曾广泛讨论过这一替代理论，讨论之处甚至在最初交锋中就被提及。
因此，为避免重复，本文题为“货币作为记账单位……”的一节简要重述英厄姆的替代路径，并指出他似乎未意识到的弱点。这些弱点恰恰产生于对货币与商品之联系的否认。
The charge of neglect is surprising, to say the least, since one of the disputants has extensively discussed this alternative theory, in places that were even mentioned in the original exchanges.

To avoid covering the same ground, therefore, Ingham’s alternative approach is briefly recapitulated in the section of this article titled ‘Money as a unit of account …’, and its weaknesses, of which he seems unaware, are identified. These weaknesses arise precisely because of the denial of the connection between money and commodities.
然而本章聚焦英厄姆介入的积极方面，即他关于“一般货币”“由社会关系构成”的主张。
这是重要洞见，只是货币所涉及的社会关系并非英厄姆假定的那些，即不是“支付承诺”或“信用—债务”关系。
与其偏好的替代（且据称被忽视的）理论一致，英厄姆把信用货币当作“一般货币”的通类是错误的。相反，构成货币的社会关系是从事交换的商品所有者之间产生的价值关系。
The focus of this chapter, however, is on the positive aspect of Ingham’s intervention, namely his claim that ‘money in general’ is ‘constituted by social relations’.
This is an important insight, except that the social relations involved in money are not those assumed by Ingham, i.e. they are not relations of ‘promise to pay’ or ‘credit–debit’.

In line with his preferred alternative (and presumably neglected) theory, Ingham is mistaken to treat credit money as the generic type of ‘money in general’. Rather, the social relations that constitute money are relations of value that emerge among commodity owners engaging in exchange.

这些关系最好被理解为从商品所有者之间的初始接触展开，其形式是“作出交换请求—获得直接交换的能力”。货币随后垄断直接交换（购买）的能力，从而充当商品所有者之间的社会纽带。商品货币与信用货币的共同内容是它们的绝对购买能力——而不是英厄姆似乎认为的某种假想的“支付承诺”。值得强调的是，这种对货币社会关系的处理大量依赖并进一步发展了马克思把货币作为一般等价物的分析。马克思主义政治经济学远非不相干，而是“一般货币”理论不可或缺的前提。

These relations are best understood as unfolding out of initial contacts between commodity owners that take the form of ‘making a request for exchange – receiving the ability to exchange directly’. Money subsequently monopolises the ability to exchange directly (buy), and thus acts as social nexus among commodity owners. The common content of both commodity and credit money is their absolute ability to buy – not some putative ‘promise to pay’, as Ingham appears to think. It is worth stressing that this treatment of the social relations of money relies heavily, and develops further, Marx’s analysis of money as the universal equivalent. Far from being irrelevant, Marxist political economy is a sine qua non for the theory of ‘money in general’.

en: 2 Money and the Labour Theory of Value

children: 按英厄姆的说法，劳动价值论是马克思货币理论的弱点：
According to Ingham, the labour theory of value is the weak point of Marx’s theory of money:
马克思的货币理论有缺陷——如同其他古典经济学家的理论一样——因为它建立在劳动价值论之上……货币与商品之间没有确定的联系。
Marx’s theory of money is flawed – like those of other classical economists – because it is grounded in the labour theory of value … There is no determinate link between money and commodities.
尽管如此，英厄姆还认为法恩与拉帕维察斯滥用了“古典”劳动价值论：
Nonetheless, Ingham also thinks that Fine and Lapavitsas have abused the ‘classical’ labour theory of value:
然而，在法恩与拉帕维察斯对马克思的解释中，我们既看不到古典劳动价值论，也看不到对近期调和古典马克思主义与信用货币现实之努力的任何参照……相反，他们提出的是本质上黑格尔式的货币起源表述。

However, in Fine and Lapavitsas’s interpretation of Marx, we are not offered the classical labour theory of value nor a reference to any of the recent efforts to reconcile classic Marxism with the reality of credit-money … Rather, they present an essentially Hegelian formulation of the origins of money.
英厄姆的“古典”（大概指“古典马克思主义”）劳动价值论究竟是什么并不清楚，法恩与拉帕维察斯如何背离了它也不明显。无论如何，下文表明劳动价值论仍是货币理论的重要洞见来源。关于价值的讨论借助法恩与哈里斯、威克斯的著作，以及宇野传统的日本马克思主义，尤其是伊藤诚。

Ingham’s ‘classical’ (presumably ‘classical Marxist’) labour theory of value is not at all clear, nor is it apparent how Fine and Lapavitsas have diverged from it. Be that as it may, it is shown below that the labour theory of value remains a vital source of insights for the theory of money. The discussion of value draws on the work of Fine and Harris, Weeks, and the Japanese Marxism of the Uno tradition, especially Itoh.

价值形式与价值实体的区分对确立“一般货币”的经济内容是根本的。不可否认，商品拥有价值形式，即它们总是彼此呈现量的等价，也就是说它们有交换价值。然而对马克思而言，资本主义条件下生产的商品还包含确定量的价值社会实体（抽象人类劳动）。对资本生产的商品而言，价值形式通过一组社会与经济过程锚定于价值实体。这些过程包括：通过经常的买卖消除商品价格之间的非传递性；工人无差别地在岗位之间流动；以及工人在工作场所受制于资本主义剥削时劳动努力的同质化。它们还包括各产业部门利润率的平均化，促使市场价格趋向生产价格。

The distinction between form and substance of value is fundamental to establishing the economic content of ‘money in general’. It is undeniable that commodities possess the form of value, that is, they always exhibit quantitative equivalences with each other, i.e. they have exchange value. For Marx, however, commodities produced under capitalist conditions also contain definite amounts of the social substance of value (abstract human labour). For commodities produced by capital, the form of value is anchored on the substance of value through a set of social and economic processes. These include the elimination of non-transitivity among commodity prices through regular buying and selling, the movement of workers indifferently between jobs and the homogenisation of work effort as workers are subjected to capitalist exploitation at the workplace. They also include equalisation of profit rates across industrial sectors inducing market prices to gravitate towards prices of production.

然而，价值形式也能脱离、甚至完全脱离价值实体。在资本主义经济中，有大量事物与活动表现为商品，却与生产出来的商品没有任何关系，例如房地产、股票、保险工具、贿赂、罚款与恩惠。这些事物与活动获得价值形式（货币价格），尽管与作为抽象劳动的价值仅有薄弱联系。同理，它们的价格强烈反映非经济的与任意的影响（心理的、政治的与制度的）。此外，在非资本主义社会，价值形式也与生产的更深层现实基本无涉，因为价值实体基本缺席。非资本主义的货币价格获得规则性与传递性，纯粹由于供求的市场关系，并由与重复交易相关的习惯支撑。

However, the form of value can also become detached, or even completely divorced, from the substance of value. In capitalist economies, there is an enormous array of things and activities that appear as commodities without bearing any relation to produced commodities, for instance, real estate, shares, insurance instruments, bribes, fines, and favours. Such things and activities acquire the form of value (money prices) despite being only tenuously related to value as abstract labour. By the same token, their prices heavily reflect non-economic and arbitrary influences (psychological, political and institutional). Moreover, in non-capitalist societies the form of value is also largely unconnected to the deeper reality of production, since the substance of value is largely absent. Non-capitalist money prices acquire regularity and transitivity due purely to market relations of demand and supply, backed by the habits associated with repeated transactions.
价值形式与价值实体的分离意味着货币出现的经济过程与价值实体无涉。等价地说，货币的出现与价值形式的发展相联系。
这一路径令英厄姆惊讶，他（错误地）觉得它是“黑格尔式的”。
相反，它既是唯物主义的又是马克思主义的，因为它表明货币是商品所有者之间社会关系的结果。

Separation of form from substance of value implies that the economic process of emergence of money is not connected to the substance of value. Equivalently, money’s emergence is associated with the development of the form of value.
This approach surprised Ingham, to whom it (erroneously) seemed ‘Hegelian’.
On the contrary, it is both materialist and Marxist because it shows money to be the outcome of social relations among commodity owners.
其基础是这样一个假定：商品所有者作为“陌生”的个人彼此接近。“陌生”一词用来表示商品所有者之间不存在可能决定其交换根本内容的先在亲属、等级、传统与道德纽带。商品所有者是无其他利害关切的个人，只力求为带到市场的商品获得等价物。同样，他们甚至不必相识，或者用新古典术语说，市场是“匿名的”。

Fundamental to it is the assumption that commodity owners approach each other as ‘foreign’ individuals. The term ‘foreign’ is used to denote the absence of pre-existing ties of kinship, hierarchy, tradition and morality among commodity owners that might determine the fundamental content of their exchanges. Commodity owners are disinterested individuals who simply aim at obtaining an equivalent for what they bring to market. Similarly, they do not even need to know each other or, in neoclassical terms, the market is ‘anonymous’.
由此，在两个“陌生”商品所有者的任何随机相遇中，必须有发起交易关系的开局首着。这一货币路径随后作出的重要理论创新，是按马克思联系“偶然”价值形式分析的“相对方—等价方”二元对立来定义开局首着。
具体说，开局首着被认为是相对方作出的交换请求，以自有商品换等价方持有的商品。
在此基础上，可以借助“相对方—等价方”的社会关系规定一个导向货币出现的分析过程。英厄姆似乎对这一货币处理的原创性感到惊讶，其关键成分重述如下。

It follows that at any random meeting of two ‘foreign’ commodity owners, there must be an opening gambit that invites trading relations to occur. An important theoretical innovation subsequently made by this approach to money is to define the opening gambit in terms of the binary opposition of ‘relative-equivalent’ analysed by Marx in connection with the ‘accidental’ form of value.
Specifically, the opening gambit is taken to be a request for exchange made by the relative party, offering own commodity for the commodity held by the equivalent party.

On this basis, an analytical process could be specified that would lead to money’s emergence by drawing on the social relations of ‘relative-equivalent’. Ingham appears to have been surprised by the originality of this treatment of money, the key components of which are recapitulated below.

zh: 3 作为购买能力垄断者的一般等价物的社会关系
en: 3 Social Relations of the Universal Equivalent as Monopolist of the Ability to Buy

children: 作出交换请求的开局首着给两个商品所有者之间的“偶然”关系以明确方向。相对方是主动方，其请求把另一方置于等价方即被动方的位置。用经济术语说，相对方宣布自有商品的交换价值由等价方持有商品的一个数量来表现。同时，等价方发现自有商品可以与相对方的商品直接交换（购买）。等价商品的这一属性是初级的“货币性”，纯粹来自相对方作出的交换请求。货币作为一般等价物，由于所有其他商品所有者自发作出的交换请求，最终垄断购买能力。

The opening gambit of making a request for exchange gives definite direction to the ‘accidental’ relationship between two commodity owners. The relative is the active party, whose request puts the other in the position of the equivalent, or passive, party. In economic terms, the relative declares the exchange value of own commodity to be represented by a quantity of the commodity possessed by the equivalent. Simultaneously, the equivalent discovers that own commodity could be exchanged directly with (buy) that of the relative. This property of the equivalent commodity is rudimentary ‘moneyness’, deriving purely from the request for exchange made by the relative. Money as the universal equivalent eventually monopolises the ability to buy, due to spontaneous requests for exchange made by all other commodity owners.

购买能力的垄断化经过相继的（分析）阶段发生，即“偶然”交换变为“扩大”、再变为“一般”、最后变为“货币”。“扩大”阶段自然跟随“偶然”阶段，因为每个商品所有者原则上都可以向任一乃至全部其他所有者作出交换请求。“扩大”阶段捕捉一个相对方对应无尽等价方的社会关系，此时商品所有者经常而频繁地进入交换过程。等价商品的所有者发现自己获得了一定程度的购买能力，哪怕只针对单一相对方。“一般”阶段与“扩大”相反，捕捉反向的社会关系，即无尽相对方对单一等价方作出请求。在“一般”阶段，除一个之外的所有商品所有者经常而频繁地向单一商品作出交换请求。该单一商品因此拥有压倒性的“货币性”。尽管如此，证明从“扩大”到“一般”阶段的分析过渡远非易事。

Monopolisation of the ability to buy occurs in successive (analytical) stages, namely as ‘accidental’ exchange becomes ‘expanded’, then ‘general’, and, finally, ‘monetary’. The ‘expanded’ stage follows naturally from the ‘accidental’, since each commodity owner could in principle address requests for exchange towards any and all others. The ‘expanded’ stage captures the social relations of one relative confronting endless equivalents, when commodity owners regularly and frequently enter the process of exchange. The owners of the equivalent commodities find that they have acquired a degree of buying ability, if only towards a single relative. The ‘general’ stage, in contrast to the ‘expanded’, captures the reverse social relations, that is, of endless relatives addressing a single equivalent. At the ‘general’ stage, all commodity owners but one make regular and frequent requests for exchange to a single commodity. The single commodity thus possesses overwhelming ‘moneyness’. Nonetheless, demonstrating the analytical passage from the ‘expanded’ to the ‘general’ stage is far from easy.
这方面的关键观察是：货币代表商品之间的极端不对称：一种商品永久置于等价方一侧，所有其他商品置于相对方一侧。但商品作为交易对象内在对称，这不利于确立为货币所特有的绝对不对称。别处发展的一个解决方案是把超经济力量（包括社会习惯）作为引致货币垄断购买能力的根本。

A key observation in this respect is that money represents extreme asymmetry among commodities: one commodity is permanently placed on the side of the equivalent and all others on the side of the relative. But commodities are intrinsically symmetric as objects of trade, and this militates against establishment of the absolute asymmetry that is characteristic of money. A solution for this problem, developed elsewhere, is to take extra-economic forces, including social custom, as fundamental to inducing monopolisation of the ability to buy by money.
这方面的重大困难是：不能直接假定社会习惯存在于商品所有者之间，因为他们本质上彼此“陌生”，因而不受亲属、宗教、等级等约束。即使商品所有者获得习惯关系，这些也仍是“陌生人”之间的关系。进一步的困难是：按上述定义的“陌生性”的存在本身，在非资本主义社会内部似乎特别不可能，那里经济活动“嵌入”权力、声望、亲属与习惯之中。

A significant difficulty in this connection is that social custom cannot be immediately assumed to exist among commodity owners, since they are essentially ‘foreign’ to each other and are thus unconstrained by kinship, religion, hierarchy, and so on. If commodity owners acquired customary relations, these would still be relations among ‘foreigners’. A further difficulty is that the very existence of ‘foreign-ness’, as defined above, seems particularly unlikely within non-capitalist societies, in which economic activity is ‘embedded’ in power, prestige, kinship and custom.
然而，“陌生性”自然盛行于资本主义交易者之间，也可能存在于非资本主义共同体与社会彼此贸易之处。这就是为什么法恩与拉帕维察斯援引马克思的论断：商品交换历史上产生于分离共同体相互接触之处。
英厄姆把这一观点斥为基于“早已被超越的历史学”，却忽视其分析重要性，而且如下文所示，他严重高估了自己偏好的替代观点的历史有效性。

However, ‘foreign-ness’ naturally prevails among capitalist traders, and could also exist at the points where non-capitalist communities and societies would engage in trade with each other. This is why Fine and Lapavitsas refer to Marx’s claim that commodity exchange historically arises where separate communities come into contact with each other.

Ingham dismisses this view as based on ‘long since superseded history’, but misses its analytical importance and, as is shown below, grossly overestimates the historical validity of his preferred alternative view.
导向货币出现的适当条件，可能存在于涉及经常贸易特定商品的“陌生人”的习惯交易链条内部。习惯上频繁交易的商品可能偶然吸引数个交换请求，导致“一般”阶段的短暂出现。显然，这在一条交易链条内可能不止一种商品发生。然而要点是：如果一种商品即使暂时成为一般等价物，其增强的购买能力会构成一种额外的（与交换相关的）使用价值，马克思称之为“形式”使用价值。
因此，该特定商品很可能吸引更多交换请求，强化其购买能力，并引来更多交换请求。一种商品垄断购买力的过程由此启动。

Appropriate conditions leading to the emergence of money are likely to exist within chains of customary transactions involving ‘foreigners’ who regularly trade specific commodities. A commodity that is customarily and frequently traded could by chance attract several requests for exchange, leading to the transient appearance of the ‘general’ stage. It is clear that this could occur for more than one commodity within a chain of transactions. The point is, however, that if a commodity became a general equivalent even temporarily, its enhanced ability to buy would constitute an additional (exchange-related) use value, which Marx called a ‘formal’ use value.

Therefore, that specific commodity would be likely to attract further requests for exchange, strengthening its ability to buy and leading to still more requests for exchange. A process of monopolisation of buying power by one commodity would be set in train.
尽管如此，要使“货币”阶段真正出现，超经济因素再次必要。商品的物理属性在这方面重要，因为耐久性、同质性、可分性与便携性对购买能力的垄断者是可取的。社会习惯也重要，因为用于财富展示的商品会更自然地与购买能力相联系。最后，货币出现之后，其持续使用仍依赖社会习惯。商品所有者自动以商品换货币，预期能在交换中获得货币。商品所有者的预期由其集体实践不断验证。

For the ‘money’ stage to emerge properly, nonetheless, extra-economic factors would again be necessary. The physical properties of commodities are important in this respect, since durability, homogeneity, divisibility and portability are desirable for the monopolist of buying ability. Social custom is also important, since commodities used for wealth display would be more naturally associated with the ability to buy. Finally, after money would have emerged, its continuous use would still rely on social custom. Commodity owners automatically offer their commodities for money, expecting that they could obtain money in exchange. The expectations of commodity owners are continually validated by their collective practice.
重述一下：马克思的价值形式分析为把“一般货币”分析推导为购买能力的垄断者提供了基础。货币与商品之间的绝对不对称部分来自经济过程，部分来自非经济关系（包括社会习惯）。货币因此凝聚了“陌生”商品所有者的社会关系。这一结果与英厄姆把货币视为由信用货币与“支付承诺”特征性社会关系构成的观点鲜明对照。英厄姆观点的弱点简要总结如下。

To recap, Marx’s analysis of the form of value provides foundations for the analytical derivation of ‘money in general’ as the monopolist of the ability to buy. The absolute asymmetry between money and commodities results partly from economic processes and partly from non-economic relations, including social custom. Money, thus, encapsulates the social relations of ‘foreign’ commodity owners. This result stands in sharp contrast to Ingham’s view of money as constituted by social relations characteristic of credit money and ‘promises to pay’. The weaknesses of Ingham’s view are briefly summarised below.

zh: 4 货币作为抽象记账单位——斯图亚特、国定论与后凯恩斯主义
en: 4 Money as Abstract Unit of Account – Steuart, Chartalism and Post-Keynesianism

children: 按英厄姆的说法，马克思对信用货币几乎无话可说，似乎只联系前资本主义形态才“理解”其特殊性质。
显然，马克思对资本主义信用工具的看法在其时代“相当常规”，他把它们当作现金（硬通货）的“替代品”。
英厄姆甚至就信用货币而言把马克思与正统货币理论归入同一阵营，与后凯恩斯主义货币理论对立。然而，英厄姆的主张是对马克思主义信用货币理论的漫画式歪曲。
According to Ingham, Marx has little to say on credit money and ‘seems to understand’ its peculiar character only in relation to pre-capitalist formations.
Apparently, Marx’s view of capitalist credit instruments was ‘quite conventional’ for his era, and he treated these as ‘substitutes’ for hard cash.

Ingham even places Marx in the same camp as orthodox monetary theory as far as credit money is concerned, in opposition to post-Keynesian monetary theory. However, Ingham’s claims are a caricature of the Marxist theory of credit money.
首先要注意的是，后凯恩斯主义货币理论的历史先声之一是银行学派，它以批评英国1844年《银行法》闻名。银行学派有精细的信用货币理论，拒绝银行券（与存款）仅是现金（黄金）替代品的观念。他们还拒绝货币数量论的正统，提出“回流规律”作为信用货币数量的调节原则。毫无疑问，马克思强烈同情银行学派。

The first thing to note is that one of the historical antecedents of post-Keynesian monetary theory was the Banking School, famous for its critique of the Bank Act of 1844 in England. The Banking School had an elaborate theory of credit money, rejecting the notion that banknotes (and deposits) were a mere substitute for hard cash (gold). They also rejected the orthodoxy of the quantity theory of money, while putting forth the ‘law of the reflux’ as regulating principle of the quantity of credit money. There is no doubt at all that Marx was strongly sympathetic to the Banking School.
因此，读到英厄姆如下断言非常令人惊讶：
It is, therefore, very surprising to read the following assertion by Ingham:
马克思持有当时常规的通货学派观点：信用工具（汇票、本票等）在合理组织的体系中不过是现金的职能替代品，或者更确切地说，应当如此。

Marx held the conventional contemporary Currency School view that credit instruments (bills of exchange, promissory notes, etc.) were, or rather should be, in a rationally organised system, no more than functional substitutes for hard cash.
事实恰恰相反。现实中，马克思区分商品货币与信用货币；明确区分单纯的法定“纸”币与信用货币；为信用货币设定了一条“循环”路径，与“回流规律”明显相似；并对货币数量论表示蔑视。

Entirely the reverse holds true. In reality, Marx differentiated between commodity and credit money; distinguished clearly between plain fiat ‘paper’ money and credit money; postulated a ‘cyclical’ path for credit money, transparently similar to the ‘law of the reflux’; and showed disdain for the quantity theory of money.
同样令人惊讶的是，英厄姆声称马克思主义与正统货币理论相似，因为两者似乎都“忽视资本主义银行通过银行贷款行为创造货币的独特性”。
马克思主义与后凯恩斯主义对银行贷款创造信用货币的分析之间的亲和性，甚至得到后凯恩斯主义领头货币理论家的承认（尽管理论分歧存在）。

It is equally surprising for Ingham to claim that Marxist and orthodox monetary theory are similar because both, apparently, ‘ignore the distinctiveness of capitalist banking’s creation of money through the act of bank lending’.

The affinity between Marxist and post-Keynesian analyses of credit money creation through bank lending is acknowledged even by leading post-Keynesian monetary theorists (theoretical differences notwithstanding).
尽管如此，英厄姆说马克思主义与后凯恩斯主义货币理论在货币出现及其与商品交换的联系问题上深刻分歧，这是对的。简言之，部分由英厄姆发展的后凯恩斯主义观点声称，货币作为抽象记账单位出现，典型地在信用领域、通过超市场权威（可能是国家）的行动。英厄姆把这一路径的理论根源追溯到德国历史学派与方法论之争（Methodenstreit），却似乎未意识到其缺陷。

Ingham is nevertheless right to state that Marxist and post-Keynesian monetary theories differ profoundly on the issue of money’s emergence and its connection with commodity exchange. In a nutshell, the post-Keynesian view, partly developed by Ingham, claims that money emerges as an abstract unit of account, typically in the realm of credit and through the action of an extra-market authority, possibly the state. Ingham traces the theoretical roots of this approach to the German Historical School and the Methodenstreit, but seems unaware of its deficiencies.
德国历史学派对货币起源确有独特观点。例如克纳普的“国定论”（chartalism）或“名目论”（nominalism）声称，货币是购买力的任意量化，是一种在量上特定的、对财富的物质索取权。
这与门格尔对立——门格尔是历史学派的主要新古典对手，他试图表明货币作为交换手段自发出现。
克纳普的论证影响了凯恩斯，凯恩斯声称货币应在理论上被理解为价格、债务与契约义务的抽象记账单位，这一主张被英厄姆多次赞许地提及。
凯恩斯还声称，货币作为抽象记账单位有远古的历史，古代美索不达米亚的“烧制砖块”即为证明。

The German Historical School certainly had distinctive views on money’s origin. Knapp’s ‘chartalism’ or ‘nominalism’, for instance, claimed that money is an arbitrary quantification of purchasing power, a quantitatively specific material claim on wealth.
This was in opposition to Menger, the chief neoclassical opponent of the Historical School, who attempted to show that money emerges spontaneously as means of exchange.

Knapp’s arguments influenced Keynes who claimed that money should be theoretically understood as abstract unit of account for prices, debts and contractual obligations, a claim that has been noted approvingly by Ingham many times.
Keynes further claimed that money as abstract unit of account is of hoary antiquity, as proven by the ‘baked bricks’ of ancient Mesopotamia.
德国历史学派论证对后凯恩斯主义的影响很强，尤其对雷——英厄姆自己的分析大量依赖雷。
对雷而言，“一般货币”似乎就是信用货币，即让交易得以进行的借方与贷方分录。
这被认为与新古典货币处理形成对照，后者聚焦交换手段职能，忽视货币更广泛的运作。
The influence of the German Historical School’s arguments on post-Keynesianism has been strong, especially on Wray, on whom Ingham relies greatly for his own analysis.
For Wray, ‘money in general’ appears to be credit-money, i.e. debit and credit entries that allow transactions to proceed.
This is supposed to stand in contrast to neoclassical treatments of money, which focus on the function of means of exchange and ignore the broader functioning of money.
英厄姆似乎未意识到其偏好的替代货币路径有发展更充分的先声。特别是，他没有讨论詹姆斯·斯图亚特爵士，后者系统区分了“记账货币”（任意的价值测量尺度）与“实体货币”（实际使用的货币）。
对斯图亚特而言，“记账货币”充当抽象计价物（numeraire），而“实体货币”产生抽象价格的实际近似。
此外，“实体货币”不必与抽象计价物有相同的名称体系，因为它只是“记账货币”的近似。同样重要的是，“实体货币”确立的实际价格不必与“记账货币”确立的观念价格一致。

Ingham seems unaware of better-developed antecedents of his preferred alternative approach to money. In particular, he offers no discussion of Sir James Steuart, who systematically differentiated between ‘money of account’ (an arbitrary scale of value measurement) and ‘material money’ (money in actual use).
For Steuart, ‘money of account’ functions as abstract numeraire, while ‘material money’ generates practical approximations of abstract prices.

Furthermore, ‘material money’ need not have the same nomenclature as the abstract numeraire, since it is only an approximation of the ‘money of account’. And not least, the actual prices that are established by ‘material money’ need not coincide with the ideal prices that are established by the ‘money of account’.
总之，对斯图亚特而言，货币既是抽象的价值测量单位，又是在实践中近似观念价格的交换手段，是一种社会约定。
在设定“记账货币”与“实体”货币的区分时，斯图亚特给了重商主义关于马库特（macoute）的神话故事以理论形式——即据称西非土著用来测量商品价值的想象金条。
In sum, for Steuart, money is a social convention both as abstract unit of value measurement and as means of exchange that approximates ideal prices in practice.

In postulating the distinction between ‘money of account’ and ‘material’ money, Steuart gave theoretical form to the mythical mercantilist stories of the macoute, i.e. of the imaginary gold bar presumably used by the natives of West Africa to measure commodity value.
把货币起源与抽象记账单位的社会发明相联系的尝试，对斯图亚特而言充满理论与经验问题，对后凯恩斯主义者依然如此。下面简要讨论其中两个，第三个更充分展开。

The attempt to associate money’s origin with the social invention of an abstract unit of account was beset with theoretical and empirical problems for Steuart, and remains so for the post-Keynesians. Two of those are briefly discussed below and a third is more fully explored.
第一，特别针对后凯恩斯主义者与英厄姆：一方面货币充当抽象记账单位、另一方面交换参与者之间发生信用关系，两者之间假定的理论联系极其薄弱。因为在理论上完全可以论证：货币在与信用毫无关系、只涉及等价物即时交换的商业交易中充当抽象计价物。这毕竟就是斯图亚特所设想的。因此即使从英厄姆的立场看，也应动用奥卡姆剃刀：如果目的是论证货币是抽象记账单位，就不必引入信用关系；单纯商品交换就够了。

First, and with particular reference to post-Keynesians and Ingham, the presumed theoretical link between, on the one side, money functioning as abstract unit of account and, on the other, credit relations occurring among exchange participants, is extremely tenuous. For it is perfectly plausible to argue in theory that money would operate as an abstract numeraire in commercial transactions which have absolutely no connection with credit, and involve only the immediate exchange of equivalents. This is, after all, what Steuart had suggested. Even from Ingham’s standpoint, therefore, Occam’s razor ought to be applied: there is no need to bring in credit relations if the aim is to argue that money is an abstract unit of account; plain commodity exchange will do.

沿同一思路，更重要的是：充当记账单位既不是货币在信用交易中的唯一职能，甚至不是最重要的职能。对信用同样根本的是货币作为支付手段的运作——除非作出离奇的假定：一切信用义务都相互清算，或者每逢到期就自动提供新的信用。但如果货币在债务清偿中充当支付手段，随之而来的是它自动充当（广义的）交换手段，尽管不是（狭义的）流通手段。此外，要充当支付手段，货币必须能够保存购买力，即必须已充当贮藏要素。简言之，信用交易是复杂经济现象，依赖货币全套经济职能，而不仅是记账单位。赋予货币作为信用关系中记账单位以特殊的理论重要性，是任意且误导的。

Along the same lines, and more significantly, functioning as unit of account is neither the only nor even the most important function of money in credit transactions. Equally fundamental to credit is the operation of money as means of payment – unless the outlandish assumption is made that all credit obligations are mutually cleared, or fresh credits are automatically extended at all times due. But if money functions as means of payment in the settlement of debts, it follows that it would automatically function as (broad) means of exchange, though not as (narrow) means of circulation. Furthermore, to function as means of payment, money must be able to preserve purchasing power, i.e. it must already function as hoard element. In short, credit transactions are complex economic phenomena that rely on the full panoply of money’s economic functions and not merely the unit of account. Assigning exceptional theoretical importance to money as unit of account in credit relations is arbitrary and misleading.
第二，尽管英厄姆作出笼统断言，却没有明确证据表明历史上存在过纯粹抽象的记账单位。
仅仅表明某一历史时期记账单位恰好与交换手段名称不同，不是这样的证据。在任何给定时期由名称不同的货币履行两种职能，是货币交换最常见的特征之一。必须证明的是历史上存在过一种起初不充当交换手段的记账货币，即拥有纯粹观念单位、仅为人类意识产物的记账货币。
Second, there is no unambiguous evidence for the historical existence of a purely abstract unit of account, despite Ingham’s sweeping assertions.

Merely showing that the unit of account happens to be differently denominated from the means of exchange during some historical period is no such evidence. The performance of the two functions by differently denominated money during any given period is one of the commonest features of monetary exchange. What must be demonstrated is the historical existence of a money of account that did not originally function as means of exchange, i.e. of a money of account with purely ideal units, the products of human consciousness alone.
在这方面，指出古埃及与巴比伦尼亚等社会的存在远不充分：它们不拥有广泛的商品交换，但货币在王室或祭司经济中充当记账单位。因为这些社会当然贸易，至少与外人贸易，其记账货币典型地包含少数产品的标准数量。这在雷主编的文集中也很明显：该文集大胆断言古代巴比伦尼亚存在观念记账货币，却只成功表明这些记账单位是白银与大麦的数量。

In this regard, it is far from sufficient to point to the existence of societies, such as in ancient Egypt and Babylonia, which did not possess broad commodity exchange but in which money functioned as unit of account in the royal or priestly economy. For these societies certainly traded, at the very least with foreigners, and their money of account typically included standard quantities of a few products. This is apparent even in the edited volume by Wray, which boldly asserts the existence of ideal money of account in ancient Babylonia but only succeeds in showing that these units of account were quantities of silver and barley.
最后，在历史中对观念记账单位的徒劳搜寻，前提是纯粹的理论混乱，这在上面概述的斯图亚特论证中很明显。毫无疑问，价格的记账体系是抽象实体，可以用观念货币单位在一张纸上完全确立。用任意数量的不同“计价物”生成这种抽象的价格名称体系，是经济学中的简单练习。此外，在货币交换实践中，特定商品的价格会在实际交换之前在其所有者头脑中观念地确定。换言之，货币的价值尺度职能当然可以由纯粹想象的或观念的货币承担。

Finally, the hapless search for an ideal unit of account in history is premised on plain theoretical confusion, which is apparent in Steuart’s argument that was summarised above. There is no doubt that the accounting system of prices is an abstract entity, which could be fully established on a sheet of paper by deploying an ideal unit of money. It is a simple exercise in economics to generate such an abstract nomenclature of price by using any number of different ‘numeraires’. Moreover, in the practice of monetary exchange, the price of a specific commodity would be ideally determined in the mind of its owner prior to actual exchange. In other words, money’s function as measure of value could certainly be undertaken by purely imaginary or ideal money.
马克思就此问题提供了有力洞见，并给出强烈警告：
Marx offered powerful insight on this issue, with a strong word of warning:
既然商品价值在金上的表现是纯粹观念的行为，我们就可以用纯粹想象的或观念的金来完成这一操作。每个商品所有者都知道……要给价值数百万镑的商品以金的估价，并不需要哪怕最微小的一点现实的金。因此，货币在价值尺度职能上只是以想象的或观念的资格起作用。这种情况引起了最荒诞的理论。

Since the expression of the value of commodities in gold is a purely ideal act, we may use purely imaginary or ideal gold to perform this operation. Every owner of commodities knows … that it does not require the tiniest particle of real gold to give a valuation in gold of millions of pounds’ worth of commodities. In its function as measure of value, money therefore serves only in an imaginary or ideal capacity. This circumstance has given rise to the wildest theories.
英尼斯被英厄姆与后凯恩斯主义者誉为其替代货币起源路径的开山鼻祖，却恰恰对价值尺度的这一方面印象过深。
他显然不知其来源，以相当大的热情但缺乏这位重商主义大师的老练，重述了斯图亚特的论证。英尼斯声称：
Innes, who is acclaimed by Ingham and the post-Keynesians as a founding father of their alternative approach to money’s origin, was unduly impressed by precisely this aspect of the measure of value.
He reproduced Steuart’s argument, apparently unaware of its source, with considerable enthusiasm but without the mercantilist master’s sophistication. Innes claimed that:
眼睛从未见过一美元，手也从未触过一美元。我们所能触到或看到的，只是支付或清偿一笔称为一美元的到期债务的承诺……抽象标准的理论并不像初看起来那样离奇，对同我讨论过这一理论的科学人士来说，它不构成任何困难。我们的一切度量都是如此。没有人见过一盎司、一英尺或一小时。

The eye has never seen, nor the hand touched a dollar. All that we can touch or see is a promise to pay or satisfy a debt due for an amount called a dollar … The theory of the abstract standard is not so extraordinary as it first appears, and it presents no difficulty to those scientific men with whom I have discussed the theory. All our measures are the same. No one has ever seen an ounce or a foot or an hour.
英尼斯的陈述正是马克思所警告之事的典型实例：货币对价值的观念测量被变成了一种“荒诞”理论，即一切货币都是信用货币。这一谬误支撑着当代后凯恩斯主义货币理论化的大部分，包括英厄姆的理论化。

Innes’s statement is an exemplary instance of precisely what Marx had warned about: The ideal measurement of value by money has been turned into a ‘wild’ theory, namely that all money is credit money. This fallacy underpins much contemporary post-Keynesian theorising on money, including that of Ingham.

然而在实际货币交换中，商品的观念价格必须变为现实，商品所有者才能在实践中获得他们观念地计算过的等价物（债权人才能收到到期应付、且未与其他债务相清算的价值）。货币无疑充当观念的价值尺度，但如果交换要有经济内容，货币还必须——而且在实践中——充当价格标准、进而充当交换手段，从而使价格成为现实。价值的观念测量只是交换过程（包括商品与债务）的第一步——在某个时点，价值还必须在实践中被测量，然后转化为实际价格。

In actual monetary exchange, however, the ideal prices of commodities must become real, if commodity owners are in practice to obtain the equivalent that they have ideally calculated (and if debt holders are to receive the value that is due to them and which has not been cleared against other debt). Money undoubtedly acts as an ideal measure of value, but if exchange is to have economic content, money must also – and in practice – act as the standard of price and then as the means of exchange, thereby rendering prices real. The ideal measurement of value is only a first step in the process of exchange (including both commodities and debts) – at some point, value must also be measured in practice and then rendered into actual price.
显然，观念价格向实际价格的转化与观念货币单位无关，完全依赖实际货币。在这方面，实际货币的货币材料与计价名称都至关重要。例如，一组给定的商品价值可以用金（作为质量）观念地测量，但如果金按惯例以索维林、法郎、美元等命名，就会产生非常不同的金的实际价格。如果价值继续用金观念地测量，而实际货币是银或青铜、各有不同名称，实际价格体系会更加不同。观念货币与实际货币的关系，在逻辑与历史上都阐明了货币起源问题。

Evidently, the transformation of ideal into actual prices has nothing to do with ideal money units, and depends entirely on actual money. In this respect, both the money stuff and the denominations of actual money are of the first importance. A given set of commodity values, for instance, might be ideally measured in gold (as mass), but would produce very different actual prices for gold, if the latter were conventionally denominated in sovereigns, francs, dollars, and so on. The actual price system would be even more different if value continued to be measured ideally in gold but the actual money comprised silver or bronze, variously denominated. The relationship between ideal and actual money casts light on the issue of the origin of money, both in logic and in history.

en: 5 The Unit of Account and the Standard of Price

children: 问题取决于货币充当价值尺度与货币充当价格标准之间的区别。马克思强调了这一区别（同时也把价值尺度与抽象劳动相联系）：

The issue hinges on the difference between money functioning as measure of value and money acting as standard of price. Marx stressed the difference (while also associating measure of value with abstract labour):
作为价值尺度，它（货币）用来把一切形形色色商品的价值转化为价格，转化为想象的金量；作为价格标准，它计量这些金量。价值尺度计量的是作为价值的商品；价格标准则相反，是以一个单位的金量计量金量，而不是用另一金量的重量计量一个金量的价值。

As the measure of value it [money] serves to convert the values of all the manifold commodities into prices, into imaginary quantities of gold; as the standard of price it measures those quantities of gold. The measure of value measures commodities considered as values; the standard of price measures, on the contrary, quantities of gold by a unit quantity of gold, not the value of one quantity of gold by the weight of another.
货币作为价值尺度，通过使用指向其货币体的自然单位——首先是质量——把商品价值转化为价格。货币作为价格标准，把一般等价物的货币体转化为标准单位，并以此设定惯例性的货币价格。因为任何社会中价格标准的各种名称确实是社会约定，即货币商品的任意数量——镑、法郎、马克。

Money as the measure of value converts commodity values into prices by using the natural units that refer to its body – mass, above all. Money as the standard of price converts the body of the universal equivalent into standard units, and in this way sets the conventional money prices. For the denominations of the standard of price in any society are indeed social conventions, i.e. arbitrary quantities of the money commodity – pounds, francs, marks.
价格标准的惯例方面，部分产生于国家或其他权威能够任意规定它，这在历史上是常态。但它也与货币材料的物理方面、以及围绕其作为单纯商品使用的社会习惯相关。于是，盐以块状出现，随生产方法与社会使用习惯而变化；布按标准尺度裁剪，随材料与使用习惯而不同；牛按头计数；成色与标准重量各异的贵金属由不同共同体按其自身传统使用。

The conventional aspect of the standard of price arises partly because the state, or some other authority, can arbitrarily dictate it, as has commonly been the case throughout history. But it is also associated with the physical aspect of the money stuff as well as with the social customs that surround its use as plain commodity. Thus, salt comes in blocks that vary with production method and social custom of use; cloth is cut in standard measures that differ according to material and habits of use; cattle is counted in heads; precious metals of variable fineness and standard weight are used by different communities according to their own traditions.
国家把任意的记账货币单位强加于社会的能力，建立在价格标准的社会约定性质之上。国家给围绕价格标准的约定以秩序，部分出于自身理由（税收与铸币税），部分为了减少数个标准并行运作不可避免的摩擦。这在铸币场合很明显，但当国家选择某种银行券、或与货币商品松散而间接联系的法定货币任意单位作为价格标准时，也没有实质不同。

The ability of the state to impose on society an arbitrary unit of the money of account rests on the socially conventional nature of the standard of price. The state gives order to the conventions surrounding the standard of price partly for reasons of its own (tax and seigniorage) and partly to lessen the inevitable frictions arising from several standards operating concurrently. This is apparent in the case of coinage, but it is not substantially different when the state chooses as standard of price a particular banknote, or an arbitrary unit of fiat money which is loosely and indirectly connected with the money commodity.
据此，英厄姆倡导的替代（国定论）路径，把国家（或其他社会构成的权威）设定价格标准的无可置疑的能力，与（想象的）任意设定价值尺度的能力混为一谈。国家当然能够创造自己的价格计价物，但这是因为已经存在一种自发价值尺度，它被惯例地命名为价格标准并充当交换手段。

In this light, the alternative (chartalist) approach advocated by Ingham confuses the undoubted ability of the state (or another socially constituted authority) to set the standard of price with an (imaginary) ability arbitrarily to set the measure of value. The state is certainly able to create its own price numeraire, but this is because a spontaneous measure of value already exists that is conventionally denominated as the standard of price and acts as the means of exchange.
诚然，创造价格计价物（由国家或其他权威）涉及一定程度的抽象。但那种抽象只指价格标准的确定，而非价值尺度。货币作为价值尺度不是抽象的（更不是观念的）——相反，它是众多商品中自发出现的一种商品。亚当·斯密尽管在这方面受到种种批评，却正确地拒绝采用斯图亚特的抽象价值尺度理论，尽管他对其完全熟悉。

To be sure, there is a degree of abstraction involved in creating a price numeraire (by the state or another authority). But that abstraction refers exclusively to determining the standard of price and not the measure of value. Money as the measure of value is not abstract (and far less ideal) – rather, it is one commodity emerging spontaneously among the many. Adam Smith, for all the criticism to which he has been subjected in this respect, was right to refuse to adopt Steuart’s theory of the abstract measure of value, despite being perfectly familiar with it.

恰恰因为货币不是观念的价值测量单位（除了经济理论家进行的一般均衡练习），英厄姆偏好的路径在试图就这种观念单位如何在实践中被设计出来给出有说服力的说明时，面临不可克服的困难。在这方面，德国历史学派的理论潮流拿不出任何堪与马克思辩证分析相比的东西，甚至比不上门格尔对货币出现的紧凑推导。例如英尼斯没有给出假想的抽象价值测量单位如何可能出现的逻辑说明。我们只剩含糊的设想：古代国家的机器不知怎么把握了价值的概念现实，进而通过固定抽象记账单位设计出连贯的价格体系。只需指出：古典政治经济学是在数百年科学努力之后、面对资本主义市场中商品不断通约的具体现实，才完成这一巨大的心智抽象功绩的。

Precisely because money is not an ideal unit of value measurement (except in general equilibrium exercises undertaken by economic theorists), Ingham’s favoured approach faces insuperable difficulties when it comes to developing a cogent account of how such an ideal unit could have been devised in practice. In this respect, the theoretical current of the German Historical School offers nothing remotely comparable to Marx’s dialectical analysis, or even to Menger’s taut derivation of money’s emergence. Innes, for instance, gives no logical account of how the putative abstract unit of value measurement could have emerged. We are left with the vague supposition that the machinery of ancient states somehow grasped the conceptual reality of value, and proceeded to devise a coherent system of prices by fixing an abstract unit of account. Suffice it to remark that classical political economy was able to perform this gigantic feat of mental abstraction only after centuries of scientific effort, and against the concrete reality of constant commensuration of commodities in capitalist markets.
值得称道的是，英厄姆意识到英尼斯在这方面的弱点。
于是他寻求更清楚的答案，并认为在格里尔森的钱币学著作中找到了。

沿德国历史学派早先探索的路线，格里尔森提出货币作为记账单位出现于赔命金（wergeld），即对社会与个人“伤害”作货币赔偿的实践。格里尔森走向这一论证，是因为他认为鉴于任何此类尝试都会产生海量双边组合，要使任何相当数量的商品通约是不可能的。于是他假定，通往不同事物通约的更可信路径，实际上由各种共同体集会提供——它们为赔偿目的确定“少数”伤害之间的等价。对格里尔森而言，货币的抽象单位是在赔命金实践中由共同体设计的。
Ingham, to his credit, realises Innes’s weakness in this respect.
Thus, he searches for a clearer answer and thinks that he has found it in the numismatic work of Grierson.

Along lines earlier explored by the German Historical School, Grierson suggested that money emerged as unit of account in wergeld, that is, in the practice of making monetary compensation for social and individual ‘injuries’. Grierson was led to this argument because he thought that it was impossible to render commensurate any significant number of commodities, in view of the huge number of bilateral combinations that would be generated in any such attempt. Thus, he assumed that a more plausible path toward commensuration of disparate things was actually provided by various communal assemblies that determined equivalences among a ‘few’ injuries for the purpose of compensation. For Grierson, the abstract unit of money was communally devised in the practice of wergeld.

格里尔森的博学著作在这方面没有说服力。首先，商品交换与货币使用在历史上可能先于赔命金实践。更重要的是，格里尔森对商品领域的价值测量过程几乎没有认识，因此把商品数量庞大与内在自然差异视为通约的不可逾越障碍。但这些假想的弱点恰恰是交换过程中（尤其在资本主义流通中）商品自发通约过程的实际优点。大量重复的双边交易（以使用价值之间的差异为前提）对确立相对价格为客观社会规范绝对必要。此类交易也为货币垄断购买能力提供必要推动。

Grierson’s erudite work is not persuasive in this regard. For one thing, commodity exchange and the use of money probably preceded the practice of wergeld in history. More significantly, Grierson showed little appreciation of the process of value measurement in the realm of commodities, and for this reason thought of the large number and the inherent natural differences of commodities as forbidding obstacles to commensuration. But these putative weaknesses are actual strengths of the spontaneous process of commodity commensuration in the course of exchange, particularly in capitalist circulation. Large numbers of repeated bilateral transactions (premised on differences among use values) are absolutely necessary to establish relative prices as objective social norms. Such transactions also provide the necessary impetus for monopolisation of buying ability by money.
实际上，问题更可能正好相反。格里尔森假定伤害比商品更容易被带入等价关系，鉴于起作用的道德、家庭、习惯、等级、伦理与其他因素，这远非显然。此外，即使一份简短的伤害清单也会产生大量双边关系，每当新“伤害”出现或旧伤害退出时都必须重新评估。共同体集会要设计连贯的抽象测量标准、从而设计赔偿，其任务将是赫拉克勒斯式的。

It is more likely, indeed, that the problem holds in reverse. Grierson’s assumption that injuries could be brought into equivalence more easily than commodities is far from obvious, in view of the moral, familial, customary, hierarchical, ethical and other factors at play. Moreover, even a short list of injuries would generate a large number of bilateral relations that would have to be reassessed whenever new ‘injuries’ emerged or old ones dropped out. The task for communal assemblies in devising a consistent abstract standard of measurement, and thus compensation, would be Herculean.
总之，与商品交换无关的“一般货币”理论深令人不满。然而其内在弱点不必然意味着需要采用新古典货币路径——后者只是把方便的交换手段插入物物交换。令英厄姆困惑的马克思主义分析避免了这些困难，表明货币作为购买能力的垄断者出现。

In sum, therefore, a theory of ‘money in general’ that would be unrelated to commodity exchange is deeply unsatisfactory. Its inherent weaknesses, however, do not necessarily imply that there is a need to adopt the neoclassical approach to money, which simply inserts a convenient means of exchange into barter. The Marxist analysis that puzzled Ingham avoids these difficulties by showing that money emerges as the monopolist of buying ability.

zh: 结论：信用货币、商品货币与“一般货币”
en: Conclusion: Credit Money, Commodity Money and ‘Money in General’

children: 本章提出的复杂问题不适合简短结论。但收尾时指出对商品货币与信用货币关系的一些分析含义是有启发的——英厄姆认为这对马克思主义货币理论构成不可解的难题。

The complex issues raised in this chapter do not lend themselves to a short conclusion. But it is instructive to finish by noting some analytical implications for the relationship between commodity and credit money, believed by Ingham to constitute an intractable problem for Marxist monetary theory.
英厄姆反复断言，马克思认为货币“本质上”是商品，因此他在贸易中寻找货币起源。

鉴于上面的讨论，显然这是错误断言。对马克思而言，货币是一般等价物或独立价值形式。没有理由假定一般等价物“本质上”是商品。相反，它可以采取多种形式——商品、法定纸币、银行券、银行存款、货币信托账户等。货币的商品形式当然是根本的，尤其因为它是货币最初在商品交换中出现的形式。但货币的任何形式都不独占代表货币“本质”的权利。相反，在其一切形式中，一般等价物仍是购买能力的垄断者，这是把其各种形式联结在一起的线索。
Ingham repeatedly asserts that Marx believes money to be ‘essentially’ a commodity, and that is why he seeks money’s origin in trade.

It is clear, in view of the discussion above, that this is an erroneous assertion. For Marx, money is the universal equivalent or independent form of value. There is no reason to assume that the universal equivalent is ‘essentially’ a commodity. On the contrary, it can take a variety of forms – commodity, fiat paper, banknotes, bank deposits, money trust accounts, and so on. The commodity form of money is certainly fundamental, not least because it is the form in which money originally emerges in commodity exchange. But none of money’s forms has exclusive rights to representing money’s ‘essence’. Rather, in all its forms, the universal equivalent remains the monopolist of the ability to buy, this being the thread that binds its forms together.
的确，这方面更严重的问题可以在英厄姆著作中找到。
在努力表明货币本质上是“社会关系”时，英厄姆觉得必须谴责任何货币是“物”的说法。然而这是误导的。货币当然是“陌生”商品所有者之间的社会关系，但它也是物。体现在物中的社会关系是资本主义市场的特征，马克思主义理论已以商品拜物教概念加以分析。
Indeed, a far more serious problem in this respect can be found in Ingham’s work.

In his effort to show that money is essentially a ‘social relation’, Ingham finds it necessary to denounce any suggestion that money is a ‘thing’. Yet, this is misleading. Money is certainly a social relation among ‘foreign’ commodity owners, but it is also a thing. Social relations embodied in things are characteristic of capitalist markets, and have been analysed by Marxist theory in terms of commodity fetishism.
货币作为物的方面在经济危机情形中特别明显：危机中资本家的社会关系可能完全不变，但由于暂时缺乏货币这个“物”，破产却很容易发生。货币的神秘与复杂大多产生于它同时是社会关系与物。此外，货币“物”采取的具体形式对货币的运作重要。

The thing-like aspect of money is particularly obvious in situations of economic crisis, during which a capitalist’s social relations might remain completely unchanged, but bankruptcy could easily occur due to temporary lack of the money ‘thing’. Much of the mystery and complexity of money arise because it is simultaneously a social relation and a thing. The particular form taken by the money ‘thing’, moreover, is important for money’s functioning.
货币各种形式之间有重大经济差异。例如资本主义商品货币内在包含价值（抽象劳动）。仅这一点就表明英厄姆主要主张的谬误，即存在适用于一切货币形式的“支付承诺体系的一般社会关系”。
资本主义商品货币不是任何人的负债，与信用过程没有必然联系：它不是支付承诺，而是最终支付工具。另一方面，信用货币确实是支付承诺，这构成它与商品货币的质的差异。把商品货币与信用货币混同为“支付承诺”是纯粹的混乱。一切货币形式有共同方面，但那是其独特的购买能力，而非某种虚构的“支付承诺”。然而要确立这一结果，必须把货币与商品相联系——恰恰是英厄姆劝人不要采取的路径。

There are significant economic differences among the forms of money. Capitalist commodity money, for instance, inherently contains value (abstract labour). This alone shows the fallacy of Ingham’s main claim, namely that there exist ‘generic social relations of the system of promises to pay’, which apply to all forms of money.

Capitalist commodity money is no-one’s liability and bears no necessary relation to credit processes: it is not a promise to pay but rather the instrument of final payment. Credit money, on the other hand, is indeed a promise to pay, and this constitutes its qualitative difference from commodity money. It is plain confusion to lump together commodity and credit money as ‘promises to pay’. There is a common aspect to all forms of money, but this is their unique ability to buy rather than some fictitious ‘promise to pay’. To establish this result, however, it is necessary to relate money to commodities, precisely the approach that Ingham advises against.
信用货币对马克思主义货币理论不构成特殊困难。
货币作为购买能力的垄断者，必然通过把购买与出售分离而充当支付手段，从而产生商业信用关系。货币也使购买力通过借贷关系在资本家之间转移成为可能。两类信用关系都由私人资本不断产生，并在资本主义经济中大量增殖。信用货币在商业资本与产业资本之间的信用交易中出现，在银行运作中获得更发展的形式，并成为货币的主导形式。
Credit money presents no exceptional difficulties for Marxist monetary theory.

Money as monopolist of buying ability necessarily functions as means of payment by separating purchase from sale, thus giving rise to trade credit relations. Money also makes possible the transfer of buying power among capitalists through relations of lending. Credit relations of both types are continually generated by private capitals and proliferate in a capitalist economy. Credit money emerges in credit transactions among commercial and industrial capitals, acquires more developed forms in the operations of banks, and becomes the dominant form of money.
资本主义信用货币当然包含支付承诺，但这也是它不同于商品货币的原因：金融机构通过发行与清偿支付承诺系统地创造与消除信用货币。尽管如此，信用货币仍是一般等价物的一种形式，共享与商品交换社会关系相联系的“一般货币”性格。

Capitalist credit money certainly comprises promises to pay but that is also why it differs from commodity money: financial institutions systematically create and eliminate credit money by issuing and settling promises to pay. Nevertheless, credit money remains a form of the universal equivalent, sharing in common the character of ‘money in general’ that is associated with the social relations of commodity exchange.
